about: How each 2026 pollster reports and treats undecided ('don't know') respondents, whether its published seats come after any allocation of them, how it prints lists below the threshold, and what is known for 2019-2022. Built by hand (round 2, agent D2) from the pollsters' statutory filings to the Central Elections Committee (gov.il 'dynamiccollectorresultitem/knesset_election<N>' PDFs; 33 filings dated 2 Sep - 19 Oct 2026 were found and read, none dated on or after 2026-10-23), press interviews and methodology notes. 'subThreshold' is checked against the filings and against data/polls.json (belowThreshold entries carrying a printed pct). Pollster names are data/polls.json's config.pollsters plus the two firms Direct Polls and Next Data. 'not found' means no statement was found; it does not mean the pollster does not allocate.

sources.filings: Central Elections Committee poll reports, https://www.gov.il/BlobFolder/dynamiccollectorresultitem/knesset_election<N>/he/Survey_<id>.pdf (the listing page is behind Cloudflare; the PDFs were located by probing N 40-127 and ids near known ones)

summary: Undecided shares reported in 2026 filings range from 0.6% (Next Data) to 10-11% (Channel 12's Midgam; Channel 13's Jewish-adult sample). Lazar (Maariv, Walla) reports 5-6%. Kantar (Kan, Israel Hayom) and Direct Polls (i24NEWS) do not report an undecided share at all.

Only Channel 12 (Midgam) states that its seats include an allocation of the undecided: its raw percentages 'do not take into account the cracking of the undecided' (פיצוח מתלבטים), so the seats do. Channel 13 asks the undecided which list they lean to and converts to seats by sector weights under a stated statistical model; whether leaners enter the seats is not stated. Every other pollster prints raw percentages of decided respondents and seats from an undisclosed weighting; none states that it allocates undecideds.

Turnout: Channel 13 runs separate Jewish-adult, young, Haredi and Arab samples and builds seats from 'the weights of the sectors in the population' (i.e. an explicit sector-turnout assumption, not disclosed). Maariv/Lazar asks likelihood to vote; Channel 13 asks it per sample. Next Data scales 2022 turnout (67.8%) and weights to a fixed 54/46 2022-coalition/opposition frame that counts 2022 non-voters with the coalition.

Below the threshold, every 2026 pollster in data/polls.json prints a percentage for the lists it shows below 3.25% (97 of the 98 such entries carry a pct; the exception is one Channel 13 entry). Direct Polls prints only lists at 1% or more and names the rest as 'under 1%'. In 2015-2022 the habit was near-universal from April 2019 on (103fm in April 2019 and one Knesset Channel poll in Sep 2019 printed 0 without a share); 2015's polls mostly did not show sub-threshold lists at all.

Maariv.firm: Lazar Research (Dr. Menachem Lazar) with the Panel4All internet panel
Maariv.undecidedReported: yes: 'the share of undecided in this poll is 5.3%' (Oct 8-9), 5.2% (Oct 14-15), 6.4% (Sep 30-Oct 1); press: 'about 5-6%' (Lazar, JPost 2026-10-16)
Maariv.undecidedTreatment: raw percentages are of decided respondents (sum to 100% without the undecided); no allocation stated. Lazar: most undecided choose within a bloc.
Maariv.seatsAfterAllocation: not stated (seats come from undisclosed weighting of decided respondents)
Maariv.turnoutQuestion: yes: 'would you come to vote' by bloc and among the undecided (78% certain overall, 37% among undecided, 74% among Arab-list voters, Oct 8-9)
Maariv.history2019_2022: Maariv used Smith and Panels Politics (Lazar) in 2019-2022. A 2021 Panels Politics poll reported 18.2% undecided; seat treatment not stated. Maariv printed sub-threshold % in 2/4 entries Apr 2019, 2/2 Sep 2019, 3/4 2020, 5/6 2021, 10/10 2022.

Walla.firm: Lazar Research with Panel4All (same firm as Maariv)
Walla.undecidedReported: no undecided share in the Oct 12 filing; asks certainty of choice ('not so sure, still undecided' 5%)
Walla.history2019_2022: Walla used Panels Politics (Apr 2019) and Midgam (Sep 2019, 2020); sub-threshold % printed 6/6, 3/3, 3/3.

Channel 12.undecidedTreatment: allocated: 'the raw data do not take into account the cracking of the undecided' (* הנתונים הגולמיים אינם לוקחים בחשבון פיצוח מתלבטים); the method is not disclosed. A Makor Rishon report (via search summary) describes pollsters assigning undecided by answers such as past vote and whether they voted.
Channel 12.seatsAfterAllocation: yes (the only pollster that says so)
Channel 12.history2019_2022: Midgam polled for Channel 12 (2019-2022); allocation statements for those years not found. Sub-threshold % printed in every entry 2019-2022.

Channel 13.firm: Shmuel Rosner (the Madad) with Panel Project HaMidgam (Dr. Ariel Ayalon), Stat-Net (Yousef Makladeh) and Askaria (Dudi Dror); statistical advice Prof. David Steinberg
Channel 13.mode: four samples: Jewish adults (online, ~600), young (~60), Haredi (~500, online), Arab (100, telephone); ~1,260 in all
Channel 13.undecidedReported: yes, per sample: Jewish adults 11.3-11.7%, Haredi 6.3-9.9%, Arab 10-11%, young 3-14% (Sep 15 - Oct 13)
Channel 13.undecidedTreatment: asks the undecided which list they lean to now (Oct 7: 38% of undecided Jewish adults still did not know); 'the seats are calculated by the sectors' weights in the population according to a statistical methodology' (undisclosed). Rosner: the algorithm places every respondent, even one who does not know, somewhere in the calculation (Maariv 2026-08-15).
Channel 13.seatsAfterAllocation: probably (Rosner's description), not stated in the filings
Channel 13.turnoutQuestion: yes, per sample: Haredi 66% certain to vote, Arab 78%, Jewish adults 78% (Oct 7). Sector turnout is an explicit, undisclosed input ('pollsters must estimate the turnout of different sectors', Rosner).
Channel 13.history2019_2022: Channel 13 used Panel Project HaMidgam and Stat-Net in 2019-2020 and Camil Fuchs in 2021-2022. Fuchs (ToI 2020-07-23) said most undecided lean centre-left and used an extra bloc question to place them. Sub-threshold % printed in every entry 2019-2022.

Kan 11.undecidedReported: no: the vote question's percentages are 'raw data' of respondents choosing a list; no undecided row
Kan 11.subThreshold: prints raw % for lists tested below the threshold (filings; data/polls.json 4/4). Kan once reported Shas+UTJ combined (Sep 28).
Kan 11.history2019_2022: Kan used TNS/Kantar in 2019-2022 (plus one Direct Polls poll in March 2019, which makes model.mjs drop Kan from the April 2019 field: see the D2 memo); sub-threshold % printed 6/6, 3/3, 3/3, 6/7, 8/8. No undecided statement found.

Israel Hayom.firm: Kantar Israel (2026); Maagar Mochot in earlier cycles
Israel Hayom.undecidedReported: no undecided row in the vote question
Israel Hayom.subThreshold: a block 'tested in the poll and did not pass the threshold' with raw % (filing Oct 15; data/polls.json 3/3)
Israel Hayom.history2019_2022: Maagar Mochot polled for Israel Hayom in 2019-2022; sub-threshold % printed 7/7, 2/4, 4/4, 5/5, 2/2. No undecided statement found.

i24NEWS.firm: Direct Polls Ltd. (Zuriel Sharon); Shlomo Filber left in June 2025
i24NEWS.mode: online respondent panel, 'probabilistic random'; 500-1,054 respondents, response rate 5.9-6.7%
i24NEWS.undecidedTreatment: not stated; raw % are of respondents naming a list
i24NEWS.subThreshold: prints % for lists at 1% or more; names lists 'sampled and under 1%' without a figure (filing Oct 1); data/polls.json 16/16 entries carry a pct
i24NEWS.history2019_2022: Direct Polls (Filber) polled for Makor Rishon and Kan (once) in 2019, for Arutz Sheva / Channel 20 and under its own name in 2020-2021, and for Channel 14 in 2022; sub-threshold % printed 4/4 (2021). No undecided statement found.

Channel 14.undecidedReported: yes, as a row inside the percentages: 4.0% (Sep 15), 1.2% (Oct 1), 0.9% (Oct 7), 0.6% (Oct 19)
Channel 14.undecidedTreatment: seats exclude the undecided; weighting by age, gender, region, religiosity, ideology and 2022 vote, with a fixed 54% 2022-coalition / 46% opposition frame (Sep 28 filing) in which 2022 non-voters are counted with the coalition (Oct 19 filing)
Channel 14.seatsAfterAllocation: no allocation stated; the near-zero undecided share is itself the anomaly
Channel 14.turnoutQuestion: 96% 'certainly vote' in its panel; projects 67.8% turnout by scaling 2022's 69.6%
Channel 14.subThreshold: a separate block 'lists that did not pass the threshold (below 3.25%)' with % (filing; data/polls.json 28/28)
Channel 14.history2019_2022: Next Data did not exist; Channel 14's 2022 polls were by Direct Polls (Filber).

Zman Yisrael.firm: Yossi Tatika (Tatika Research and Media) with the Adgenda panel (Roi Schindler)
Zman Yisrael.mode: panel, n = 500, stratified by age, religion, gender and region (zman.co.il 2026-09-17)

Yedioth Ahronoth.status: no 2026 polls in data/polls.json and no 2026 CEC filing found
Yedioth Ahronoth.history2019_2022: Midgam polled for Yedioth in 2015 and April 2019; sub-threshold % printed 2/2 (Apr 2019). No undecided statement found.

Ynet.status: no 2026 polls in data/polls.json and no 2026 CEC filing found

Makor Rishon.status: no 2026 polls in data/polls.json and no 2026 CEC filing found
Makor Rishon.history2019_2022: Direct Polls (Apr 2019) and Panels Politics (2020) for Makor Rishon; sub-threshold % printed 6/6 and 1/1.

Haaretz.status: no 2026 polls in data/polls.json and no 2026 CEC filing found
Haaretz.history2019_2022: Dialog (Camil Fuchs) for Haaretz in 2019-2021; sub-threshold % printed 1/1 (Apr 2019).

DRI institute (independent).note: online panel, n ≈ 2,185; raw % and seats, no undecided row; not in config.pollsters

Maagar Mochot (Prof. Yitzhak Katz) for '.note: panel + telephone, n ≈ 535; reports a 'don't know' row and seats 'with weighting'; the subject of a petition over undisclosed processing (Maariv 2026-10-08); not in config.pollsters

aChord Center (iPanel).note: attitude survey; explicitly no conversion to seats

history.gershuniAylho2015: Project 61 audit of 2006-2013: 20-50% of respondents undecided in campaign polls; undecided respondents name a large party as a camp label; Arabs and Haredim answer phone polls less. https://www.timesofisrael.com/how-a-28-year-old-analyst-is-fixing-israels-polls/
history.fuchs2020: Camil Fuchs: most undecided lean centre-left; he places them with an extra bloc question. https://www.timesofisrael.com/top-pollster-challenges-assertion-right-wing-bloc-has-been-gaining-ground/
